absent: Numeric values, bit positions, and full mask definitions for GFP, SLAB, OBJEXTS, MEMCG_DATA, OO_SHIFT, OO_MASK, and SL_pfmemalloc symbols.
Complete struct definitions and sizes for kmem_cache, slab, kmem_cache_node, slab_obj_iter, freelist_counters, track, slabobj_ext, and codetag reference.
Page allocator internals behind frozen page primitives and the behavior of alloc_hooks instrumentation.
Lock ordering, interrupt state, and concurrency contracts beyond the observed node list_lock usage and freelist atomic update assertion.
Implementations of cross dossier helpers for memory fill, list handling, atomics, bit operations, lock validation, logging, stack dump, and low memory tests.
Cache lifecycle, slab destruction, object free, reclaim, migration, accounting teardown, and sanitizer and profiling subsystems outside the routed allocation fragments.
Configuration conditions selecting active versus inert build variants for tracking, debugging, extensions, and full list accounting.

findings.text: A shared sanitizer accepts allocation request flags, removes combinations that must never reach the slab layer, emits a diagnostic with a stack trace, and returns the cleaned value for continued use. Creation paths invoke it only when a forbidden combination is present.

A leak detector helper marks a supplied address as intentionally retained so later scans do not report it. It ignores absent or error encoded addresses and acts only while the detector is active, delegating the state change to an internal gray marking operation.

Several slab helpers are visible beyond their defining file, with build dependent active or inert variants. They cover debug pattern fill of a new slab, adjustment of an object base past left redzone padding, and allocation of per object extension vectors, where one build always reports success without acting.

Three preprocessor wrappers expose frozen page allocation with instrumentation hooks. They distinguish allocation on a specified node, allocation on any node, and a lock free variant used when spinning is forbidden, each forwarding to a corresponding internal implementation.

Permission to spin is the absence of a no lock marker in allocation control flags. The predicate result selects blocking versus try lock behavior on node lists, selects page allocator entry, and selects deallocation and leak notification paths.

Order and object count share one packed value. Order occupies high bits accessed by shifting, while object count occupies low bits accessed by masking. Creation logic compares configured and minimum orders and sizes slabs from the decoded count.

A cache is a kmalloc cache when a dedicated marker flag is present. It counts as normal only when none of several exclusion flags for direct memory access, accounting, reclaim accounting, or disabled extensions is present. The normal property steers extension vector placement to avoid recursion.

Slab creation rejects invalid request flag combinations by sanitizing them, warns when a constructor is combined with zeroing, intersects the request with globally allowed and cache contributed flags, and restricts the surviving set to reclaim and constraint categories before delegating.

A newly acquired slab starts with cleared counters, a decoded object capacity, a back link to its cache, and initialized extension state. Page conversion marks the page as slab memory and propagates a low memory allocation marker to the slab descriptor when present on the page.

Need for per object extensions is build dependent. One build never needs them. The other refuses them for caches marked as extension free, otherwise requires them when memory control accounting is online for accounted caches or when allocation profiling is active.

Early extension storage prefers unused tail space inside the slab when offset plus size fits, otherwise uses space inside each object when the cache permits it, and otherwise does nothing. Offsets account for debug information, user tracking, original size, and sanitizer metadata, with inert builds reporting no fit and zero offset.

Object setup combines debug preparation, sanitizer initialization, and optional construction. Debug preparation is inert unless redzone or poisoning or user tracking is enabled, in which case it initializes redzone state and clears a pair of allocation records. Slab wide debug fill applies a poison pattern only when poisoning is enabled.

Reuse from partially occupied slabs first targets the requested node, substituting the current node when no node was requested. A miss falls back to any node unless the request is pinned to one node, and entries that fail a low memory compatibility check are skipped during the scan.

Freelist publication uses an atomic compare exchange over pointer plus counters, selecting a wide or narrow primitive from cache capabilities, with backoff and failure accounting on contention. Fresh slab freelists are null terminated chains over all but the first object, enumerated sequentially or in randomized order with wrap handling.

Successful creation charges the owning node by the slab byte size derived from order and ensures extension storage for accounted caches that lack it. Node slab and object totals advance atomically in one build and are inert in another, while full list membership is maintained only when user tracking is enabled.

Extension allocation failure can be recorded with a distinctive marker installed only when no vector is present. A later successful vector observes that marker and, when code tagging is active, initializes its per object tag references to an empty state to suppress later warnings. One build never records or handles such failures.

Publication of a fresh slab serializes on the owning node list lock with interrupts saved. Blocking acquisition is used when spinning is allowed, while a nonblocking attempt is used otherwise, discarding the new slab and reporting failure when the attempt loses.

Scanning and popping from a node partial list holds the same node list lock with interrupts saved. The non spinning caller uses a nonblocking acquisition and abandons the scan immediately on contention, relying on a racy preliminary check of partial count to avoid needless locking.

Atomic freelist and counter updates require interrupts disabled on non realtime builds, verified by a lock validation assertion. The operation itself is lock free and may be retried by callers that already hold the node list lock to exclude transitions to fully free state.

Observed slab state includes combined counters, object capacity, in use count, freelist head, frozen marker, cache back link, node list linkage, extension pointer with in object and object control group markers, and a low memory flag. Debug failure transitions set all objects in use with an empty freelist and frozen state.

Observed cache state includes configured and minimum order object packs, allocation flags, behavior flags, optional constructor, object size, left redzone padding, and an optional randomization sequence. Flags select debugging, accounting, extension policy, atomic update width, and kmalloc identity.

Observed per node cache state includes an interrupt protected list lock, partial and full slab lists, a racy partial count, and atomic totals for slabs and objects. List membership changes and counter updates occur while holding the list lock.

Allocation iteration keeps a start address, position, randomization enablement, sequence length, and byte limit. Atomic freelist state pairs a pointer with counters that include use count. User tracking stores paired allocation records per object, and extension vectors are sized as per object stride times object capacity.

Creation first attempts the configured order with failure tolerant modifiers that suppress warnings and retries and adjust reclaim behavior under pressure. On failure it retries once at minimum order with the unmodified request flags and reports overall failure only if the second attempt fails.

A fresh slab with one reserved object becomes partial when capacity exceeds one and full otherwise. Debug rejection leaks the slab without publication, while lock contention on the non spinning path frees the slab without discard processing.

Extension vectors move among absent, present, and allocation failed states. A brand new slab installs its vector without synchronization, while a shared slab reuses an existing vector when present or installs a new one with atomic compare exchange and retry, freeing the surplus on loss.

Allocation time debugging has active and always successful builds. The active build validates slab integrity, pointer membership, and object redzone state when consistency checking is enabled, records tracing and size metadata on success, and quarantines the slab on failure.
The creation entry enforces request flag hygiene for reclaim and constraint categories before delegating to the allocator that establishes a fully initialized and accounted slab.

Allocation combines reuse and fresh carving. Reuse honors node preference with fallback to any node. Fresh carving reserves initial object capacity from a new slab and publishes the slab for shared use after validation.
Page acquisition selects a frozen page primitive from spinning permission and node selection and establishes a slab descriptor that records slab identity and low memory origin.
Combining a cache constructor with a zeroing request triggers a one time warning, because zeroing memory that a constructor will immediately initialize is wasteful and may hide constructor omissions.
Request flags containing slab forbidden combinations are stripped with a warning and stack trace to identify the caller. Callers must fix the flag selection rather than rely on silent correction.

Extension vectors for normal kmalloc caches must come from caches that themselves carry no extensions, otherwise vector allocation would recurse. Debug builds validate that the backing cache belongs to an allowed family.

Concurrent installers of an extension vector on a shared slab race safely only through atomic compare exchange with retry and reuse of the winner. Clearing of control group related request bits before vector allocation prevents unintended accounting inheritance.

Non spinning callers must handle lock contention as a normal outcome. A fresh slab is discarded and freed on publication contention, while a partial scan simply returns no object, allowing the caller to fall back to another path.

Suspected freelist or redzone corruption during allocation quarantines the slab by marking all objects used and freezing it, leaking the memory deliberately to avoid handing corrupted objects to callers.

Slabs created from emergency reserves are usable only for compatible requests. The partial scan skips incompatible slabs based on a propagated per slab marker, so such memory never leaks to unsuitable callers.

Randomized object enumeration must tolerate slabs whose capacity is smaller than the configured count and wrap its position safely. Non spinning contexts use a per cpu generator that may be disturbed by interrupts without breaking correctness.

Allocation control symbols SLAB_ALLOC_NOLOCK and SLAB_ALLOC_NEW_SLAB and SLAB_ALLOC_NO_OBJ_EXT distinguish spinning permission and brand new slab handling and suppression of extension allocation. Their presence selects locking and publication and vector source behavior.

Flag hygiene uses GFP_SLAB_BUG_MASK with GFP_RECLAIM_MASK and GFP_CONSTRAINT_MASK to identify forbidden and surviving request bits. Creation also observes __GFP_NOWARN and __GFP_NORETRY and __GFP_NOFAIL and __GFP_DIRECT_RECLAIM and __GFP_NOMEMALLOC and __GFP_RECLAIM for warning and retry and reclaim behavior.

Cache behavior symbols SLAB_KMALLOC and SLAB_CACHE_DMA and SLAB_ACCOUNT and SLAB_RECLAIM_ACCOUNT and SLAB_NO_OBJ_EXT and SLAB_OBJ_EXT_IN_OBJ and SLAB_STORE_USER and SLAB_RED_ZONE and SLAB_POISON and SLAB_CONSISTENCY_CHECKS plus __CMPXCHG_DOUBLE and __OBJECT_POISON select kmalloc identity and accounting and extension and debugging and atomic update roles.

Layout symbols OO_SHIFT and OO_MASK define packing of order and count. State symbols POISON_INUSE and OBJEXTS_ALLOC_FAIL and MEMCG_DATA_OBJEXTS and OBJEXTS_FLAGS_MASK and OBJCGS_CLEAR_MASK and NUMA_NO_NODE and SL_pfmemalloc mark debug fill and extension status and node selection and low memory origin.
